episodeTitle.en: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe
episodeTitle.zh: 通过了解大脑来提升战略、影响力和决策力 | 埃文·拉普安特

guestBioOfficial.en: Evan LaPointe is the founder of CORE Sciences, which teaches companies and individuals how our brains work and how that translates to improved collaboration, better products, faster decision-making, and more growth. Previously, Evan was the co-founder of Satellite, the fourth-largest analytics product on the internet today (it mostly runs behind the scenes, and pretty much everyone listening will have used it today without knowing it), which was acquired by Adobe, where he later ran product strategy, innovation, and long-range thinking for Adobe’s digital experiences business. In our conversation, we discuss: • The three different systems of the brain
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃文·拉普安特是CORE Sciences的创始人，该公司教会企业和个人我们的大脑如何运作，以及如何将其转化为更好的协作、更优质的产品、更快的决策和更多增长。此前，埃文是Satellite的联合创始人，Satellite是当今互联网上第四大分析产品（它主要在幕后运行，几乎每个听众今天都会在不知情的情况下使用过它），后被Adobe收购，他随后在Adobe的数字体验业务中负责产品战略、创新和长期规划。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 大脑的三个不同系统

title.en: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe
title.zh: 通过了解大脑来提升战略、影响力和决策力 | 埃文·拉普安特

summary.en: Evan frames the brain as a college campus with different 'departments,' and argues most people over-rely on the risk-averse 'history department' instead of routing problems to the more experimental, creative parts of the mind for dramatically better answers. He shows how this lens improves concrete work: becoming more influential by choosing the 'character' you play (devil's advocate, stress-tester, and so on), running better meetings, and increasing focus. A central, refreshingly blunt takeaway is that before anything else you must ask whether you are a 'miserable experience' to work with, because a toxic presence undermines everything else. The episode blends neuroscience with highly actionable tactics for building more productive relationships and making faster, smarter decisions.
summary.zh: Evan 把大脑比作一个有大大小小不同“部门”的大学校园，并指出大多数人都过度依赖那个规避风险的“历史系”，而不是把问题交给大脑中更具实验精神、更有创造力的部分，从而错过明显更好的答案。他用这个视角改进具体的工作：通过选择自己扮演的“角色”（比如唱反调的人、压力测试者等）来提升影响力、把会议开得更好、更专注。一个直白又核心的洞见是：在考虑其他一切之前，你必须先问自己是不是一个“让人难受的共事对象”，因为糟糕的个人状态会毁掉其他所有努力。这一期把神经科学和高度可操作的实战方法结合在一起，帮助你建立更高效的人际关系，并做出更快、更明智的决策。
